name: The Hague University of Applied Sciences
summary: Hogeschool in The Hague with 13 English bachelor's, from law and European studies to UX design; computing and electronics are taught in Delft.

ib.text: A full IB Diploma (24+ points, 3 HL subjects with 12+ points between them, TOK passed) opens both the 4-year and the 3-year programmes. English at HL exempts you from an English test.

programmes.name: Applied Computer Science
programmes.about: Making machines, computers and networks work together, from embedded systems to software, in a three-year programme taught in Delft's tech hub, preparing you for high-tech firms or a master's.
programmes.overview: The first year moves through Python and databases, C programming with networks and hardware, cybersecurity, and then data science, cloud computing and responsible AI. After year one you pick embedded software development or cybersecurity. Learning is hands-on, with lab work, company-based projects and continuous assessment in place of big exams. Year two includes a minor or work placement, and year three brings a research project and a graduation thesis. Graduates work as IoT developers, cybersecurity analysts, cloud architects or software developers, or continue to a master's in applied or technical universities.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the entry requirements and you are admitted. 2027 deadlines not yet published; in 2026 EU/EEA applicants could apply until late July.

programmes.name: Electrical and Electronic Engineering
programmes.about: Microchips, sustainable energy and intelligent hardware in a three-year Delft programme, with project work alongside semiconductor companies such as ASML.
programmes.overview: Year one covers digital systems, electricity, magnetism, energy, drive systems and programming, alongside mathematics and physics. In year two you go deeper into embedded systems, energy technology and electronics through semester-long projects such as offshore wind turbine designs. Teaching mixes lectures, practicals in small groups and project teams of two to six students working on fictional cases or real company assignments. In year three you choose an internship or a minor in robotics, entrepreneurship or energy transition, then finish with a six-month graduation project at a company. Typical jobs include embedded systems, electronics design, control and test engineering.

needs.note: The maths exam must be passed.

programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the entry requirements and you are admitted. 2027 deadlines not yet published; in 2026 EU/EEA applicants could apply until late July.

programmes.name: European Studies
programmes.ib: French, German or Spanish throughout, at beginner or advanced level. A separate 3-year fast track, with its own page, is open to full IB Diploma holders.
programmes.about: Business, politics and law of Europe combined with professional skills and a modern language (French, German or Spanish), plus an exchange abroad and an internship.
programmes.overview: Year one introduces Europe's institutions, law, politics, business and intercultural communication, alongside a modern language of your choice. Later years turn to sustainability in Europe, then peace, security and prosperity, and finally diversity in Europe. Work is project-based, with assignments such as policy advice, marketing plans and strategy documents rather than mainly exams. You spend five months on an exchange abroad, can add a minor, and in the final year complete a capstone project, a five-month internship and a graduation research project. Graduates become policy officers, sustainability advisors, lobbyists, export managers or communications professionals, and many go on to a master's.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the entry requirements and you are admitted. 2027 deadlines not yet published; in 2026 EU/EEA applicants could apply until late July.

programmes.name: Industrial Design Engineering
programmes.ib: You must have passed your IB Maths exam (AA or AI).
programmes.about: Designing products by co-creating with users and stakeholders, following one design process across very different projects, from playground equipment to interactive museum exhibits.
programmes.overview: The first year is built around integrated design projects, with courses in sketching, prototyping, studio work, user research, business planning and design software. Teaching is learning by doing: roughly 45 percent of the curriculum is project work, supported by workshops, a 3D protolab and laser cutters. Group projects for real clients such as Bosch, Ahrend and Rabobank are shown at end-of-semester design expos. In year three you take a minor, for example Design with Nature or Packaging Design and Innovation, or do an internship or exchange, then complete a graduation project for an external client. Graduates work as product, service or interaction designers, user researchers and innovation managers.

needs.note: The maths exam must be passed.

programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the entry requirements and you are admitted. 2027 deadlines not yet published; in 2026 EU/EEA applicants could apply until late July.

programmes.name: International and European Law
programmes.about: International, European and private law taught in The Hague, the city of international courts, with practical legal skills such as case analysis and legal drafting from year 1. Awards a Bachelor of Laws.
programmes.overview: You start with introductions to law, international law, private law and EU law, learning to write, reason and negotiate like a lawyer. Later years add international criminal law and corporate and trade law, and in year three you pick four electives such as corporate governance or climate and natural resources. Teaching leans on professional scenarios and moot court, where students argue for fictional clients, and many enter international moot competitions. You can take a minor or a semester abroad, and the fourth year combines an internship of at least 100 working days with an applied research project. Graduates become corporate lawyers, compliance officers, EU policy advisors or legal advisers in government, or go on to a master's abroad.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the entry requirements and you are admitted. 2027 deadlines not yet published; in 2026 EU/EEA applicants could apply until late July.

programmes.name: International Business
programmes.ib: Maths, Economics or Business Management passed. A separate 3-year track, with its own page, is for VWO-level diplomas such as the full IB.
programmes.about: How companies create value across borders: economics, marketing, finance, operations and supply chain, studied with classmates from 40+ countries and specialisations such as finance and accounting.
programmes.overview: Year one lays foundations in marketing, accounting, economics, finance and operations, with communication and teamwork skills alongside. Year two deepens finance, marketing, operations and corporate social responsibility through analytical projects. In year three you choose a specialisation in finance, operations or marketing, and can add a minor or electives and study abroad. Lectures, workshops and group projects dominate, with work gradually becoming more independent. The fourth year is a semester-long internship at an international organisation followed by a graduation project on a real business problem. Graduates work as financial analysts, digital marketers, procurement analysts or logistics coordinators.

needs.note: One of Maths, Economics or Business Management passed.

programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the entry requirements and you are admitted. 2027 deadlines not yet published; in 2026 EU/EEA applicants could apply until late July.

programmes.name: International Communication Management
programmes.about: Project-based training in international communication: media campaigns, reputation, conferences and influencing target groups, graduating with a portfolio of professional work. Runs in three years.
programmes.overview: You begin with global communication contexts, intercultural awareness, organisational communication, research methods, design thinking and marketing basics. Year two turns to public relations, public affairs and communication for the Sustainable Development Goals, and you choose a thematic minor or an exchange abroad. Teaching is mostly project work for real clients such as multinationals, NGOs and The Hague Municipality. Year three covers strategic communication and change management, and ends with a graduation internship of about 15 weeks. Graduates work as communication consultants, PR officers, marketing coordinators or social media managers, and about half continue to a master's.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the entry requirements and you are admitted. 2027 deadlines not yet published; in 2026 EU/EEA applicants could apply until late July.

programmes.name: International Financial Management & Control
programmes.ib: IB Maths plus Economics or Business Management passed, then a 30-45 minute interview in English. A separate 3-year track is open to full IB Diploma holders.
programmes.about: Accounting, risk management, strategy and decision-making applied to real companies, from pricing for a small brand to budgeting for a multinational.
programmes.overview: Year one covers financial accounting, finance and investments, marketing and Excel; year two adds cost accounting, corporate finance, risk management and sustainability. Year three opens with an internship of about six months in the Netherlands or abroad, followed by strategic and risk management. In year four you choose two minors, such as blockchain, data science or FinTech, or study at a partner university, then finish with a second internship and a graduation project. Case studies, study visits and guest speakers support the teaching. Pre-master options lead to master's programmes in accounting, auditing and finance, and graduates work as controllers, analysts and auditors.

needs.note: The maths exam must be passed.

programmes.selectionNote: An eligibility check, then a compulsory interview in English about whether the programme fits you. 2027 deadlines not yet published.

programmes.name: International Public Policy and Leadership
programmes.about: How governments and NGOs tackle climate change, inequality and human rights, learned by writing policy briefs, running campaigns and organising your own global-issues conference in year 2.
programmes.overview: The programme is organised around five professional areas: advising, advocacy, evaluation, organisation and management, and project-based working, drawing on politics, law, economics and international relations. In year two you plan, run and evaluate your own conference on a global issue. Year three offers three tracks: European governance with a Brussels trip, peace, justice and human rights, or global governance and development. Teaching mixes seminars, study visits and group projects that produce policy briefs and speeches. Year four brings a 20-week internship and a professional product or thesis. Graduates work in NGOs, ministries and international organisations, or take a pre-master toward public administration at Leiden.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the entry requirements and you are admitted. 2027 deadlines not yet published; in 2026 EU/EEA applicants could apply until late July.

programmes.name: Process & Food Technology
programmes.ib: The 3-year track, with its own page and open to full IB Diploma holders, needs IB Maths and Chemistry passed.
programmes.about: Chemical and food production processes studied in labs and a kitchen, from cheese-making and brewing in year 1 to sustainable, biobased products in projects set by industry.
programmes.overview: Year one combines chemistry, mathematics, biotechnology and basic process technology, applied at once in labs and projects such as water treatment and cheese making. In year two you design sustainable production processes with industry partners, using simulation software. Year three offers a minor, for example Food Product Design, and an internship at a company, engineering firm or research institute. In the final year you specialise in food industry processes or chemical process technology and write a thesis at a partner company. Field trips to plants and breweries support the lectures. Graduates work as process or food technologists, product developers and quality or safety engineers, or move on to a master's.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the entry requirements and you are admitted. 2027 deadlines not yet published; in 2026 EU/EEA applicants could apply until late July.

programmes.name: Safety and Security Management Studies
programmes.about: Terrorism, crime, industrial hazards and hybrid threats: assessing risks and managing security, with an optional minor in intelligence collection and analysis.
programmes.overview: Year one covers international law, criminology, psychology, economics and policy making. Year two focuses on industrial safety and international security, with crisis management, geopolitics and conflict studies. In year three you choose three minors from options such as intelligence collection and analysis, health, safety and environmental management, human security, and counterterrorism. Guest lecturers from the intelligence community and military, and visits to military bases and prisons, support the teaching. Year four is an international internship, for example at NATO or OPCW, then a thesis. Graduates work as security risk analysts, policy advisors and security managers, or continue to crisis and security management at Leiden.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the entry requirements and you are admitted. 2027 deadlines not yet published; in 2026 EU/EEA applicants could apply until late July.

programmes.name: Sport Studies | International Sport Management
programmes.ib: An interview is a compulsory part of the application.
programmes.about: How sport is managed and why it matters to society, with leadership training and the idea of sport as a driver of social change running through a three-year programme.
programmes.overview: Year one introduces sport and society, international sport management, leadership, ethics, research methods, event management and sport development. Year two moves to strategic management, sport policy, marketing, finance, sponsorship and people management. Learning is practical: students co-organise real events with sponsors, take study trips to European sport organisations and work on applied cases. In year three you shape your own route with a minor, an internship or an exchange abroad, and the final stage is a graduation challenge for a real sports organisation and a thesis. Graduates work as sport development officers, marketers, sponsorship managers and event coordinators.
programmes.selectionNote: An eligibility check, then a compulsory interview in English about whether the programme fits you. 2027 deadlines not yet published.

programmes.name: User Experience Design
programmes.about: Designing with technology around what people really need, beyond screens and apps, tackling questions such as liveable cities and a green future through hands-on experiments.
programmes.overview: The first year covers UX and interaction design, research methods, the psychology of experience and programming, with web technologies, mobile platforms, Arduino and sensors. You learn by working on projects for real clients such as Philips, IKEA and Google, in workshops equipped for prototyping, and a field trip to the Ars Electronica Festival in Linz is included. Later years add an internship at a design agency or tech company, a minor such as game development or photography, and an optional exchange. The degree ends with an independent graduation project. Graduates work as UX designers and researchers, interaction and service designers, and front-end or mobile developers.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the entry requirements and you are admitted. 2027 deadlines not yet published; in 2026 EU/EEA applicants could apply until late July.

notes: European Studies, International Business, Financial Management & Control and Process & Food Technology each run a 4-year and a faster 3-year track, and a full IB Diploma qualifies you for either.

Six degrees (Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Industrial Design, Communication, Sport Management, UX Design) run only as 3-year programmes for VWO-level diplomas, which a full IB Diploma meets.
THUAS has not yet published its 2027 deadlines; for 2026 entry non-EU applicants had to apply by 1 May and EU/EEA applicants by 31 July (2026 dates).
